questions.question: Present the Statement of Comprehensive Income of Ngcobo and Venter Traders for the year ended 28 February, from sales down to net profit, and explain why the partners' salaries are absent from it.
questions.expected_answer: Sales R2 880 000 less cost of sales R1 800 000 gives gross profit of R1 080 000. Add other operating income — rent income R45 600 and commission income R26 400, together R72 000 — for gross operating income of R1 152 000. Less operating expenses of R600 000: salaries and wages R312 000, depreciation R66 000, trading stock deficit R3 400, bank charges R11 200, insurance R24 800, telephone R19 600, provision for bad debts adjustment R600, bad debts R7 400 and sundry expenses R155 000. Operating profit R552 000, less the R24 000 interest capitalised on the Sisonke Bank loan, gives net profit for the year of R528 000. Partners' salaries, interest on capital and the bonus are appropriations — the owners dividing the measured profit among themselves — so they belong in the current accounts note, never among expenses: expenses pay outsiders, appropriations settle matters between insiders. The heading reads FOR the year ended, because the statement covers a period.

questions.question: Assemble the Statement of Financial Position on 28 February in its two towers and demonstrate that they balance.
questions.expected_answer: Assets: non-current — fixed assets at carrying value R755 000, detailed in the note. Current assets R420 400: inventories R217 500; trade and other receivables — debtors R64 000 less the R3 200 provision giving R60 800, plus prepaid expenses R3 100 and accrued income R1 900; cash and cash equivalents — bank R134 600 and cash float R2 500. Total assets R1 175 400. Equity and liabilities: owners' equity R889 800 — capital accounts R800 000 plus current accounts R89 800; non-current liabilities — the Sisonke Bank loan at its closing balance of R185 000, capitalised interest included; current liabilities R100 600 — creditors R94 200, accrued expenses R2 300 and income received in advance R4 100. Total equity and liabilities R1 175 400, equal to total assets — the accounting equation published. Classification follows the twelve-month test, and debtors and fixed assets appear net, with the workings shown in the notes.

questions.question: Reconstruct the fixed assets note and the current accounts note, and show how each meets its figure on the face of the statement.
questions.expected_answer: Fixed assets note: land and buildings at R560 000 with no depreciation, since land does not wear out. Vehicles: cost R285 000, accumulated depreciation R114 000 at the start, depreciation for the year R57 000 at 20 percent on cost, closing accumulated depreciation R171 000, carrying value R114 000. Equipment: cost R150 000, accumulated depreciation R60 000 at the start, depreciation R9 000 at 10 percent on the diminishing balance, closing carrying value R81 000. The carrying values add to R755 000 — the face figure. The note also states the depreciation policy in words, as consistency requires. Current accounts note, per partner: opening balances R9 600 for Ngcobo and minus R6 800 for Venter; interest on capital R40 500 and R31 500; salaries R150 000 and R168 000; bonus nil and R12 000; profit shares R72 000 and R54 000; drawings minus R224 000 and minus R217 000; closing balances R48 100 and R41 700, together R89 800 — the current accounts line inside equity on the face.
